blocks.text:
After breakfast, transfer from Puerto Natales (Chile) to El Calafate (Argentina), across mountains and steppe where you may see guanacos, hares and foxes. On arrival, transfer to the hotel. On the shore of Lago Argentino, El Calafate is the gateway to Los Glaciares National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1981: about 40% of the park is covered by ice fields, with 47 major glaciers, 13 of which flow east to feed Lake Viedma and Lago Argentino, and some 190 smaller glaciers.

Evening · Guided jeep tour “Nativo Experience” with dinner in a cave. On this anthropological journey through time, learn how Indigenous peoples and later settlers lived in these lands, driving along Lago Argentino to caves where the Indigenous peoples of Patagonia left paintings thousands of years ago, before an unforgettable dinner of traditional dishes in the caves.

blocks.text: Breakfast. Excursion to the Perito Moreno Glacier, 80 km from El Calafate in the south-west of Lago Argentino. Named after the great 19th-century Argentine explorer, it is one of the few glaciers in the world that is not retreating. From time to time its 60-metre ice front releases walls of ice the size of buildings into Brazo Rico or the Canal de los Témpanos. Periodically it advances to the Magallanes Peninsula and dams Brazo Rico, whose level rises considerably until the water carves through the ice and the barrier collapses: a breathtaking sight.
